To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have fabricated organic/inorganic hybrid bulk heterojunction solar cells based on P3HT:PC60BM and ZnO nanowire array grown on flexible transparent PET substrates and the device exhibited an efficiency of 1.8%.
we have successfully fabricated flexible hybrid solar cells on PET substrates using ZnO nanorods as an electron transport layer.

we fabricated the flexible solar cell with a structure of PET/ ITO/ZnO thin films/ ZnO nanorods /P3HT:PC _{60} BM/Ag and it exhibits the power conversion efficiency of 1.7% under 100 mW/cm ^{2} AM1.5G illumination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of flexible organic/inorganic hybrid bulk heterojunction solar cells on a transparent substrate.
the fabrication of flexible organic/inorganic hybrid bulk heterojunction solar cells based on ZnO nanorods and the conjugated polymer/fullerenes.
the fabrication and characterization on flexible organic/inorganic hybrid photovoltaic devices based on conjugated polymers and nanocrystalline oxide semiconductor materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fabrication of organic/inorganic solar cells based on the conjugated polymer/fullerenes blend and ZnO nanowire arrays on a flexible transparent substrate is possible.
we have successfully fabricated flexible solar cells based on ZnO nanorods and P3HT:PC61BM photoactive layer on a flexible PET substrate.

the fabrication of organic/inorganic solar cells based on the conjugated polymer/fullerenes blend photoactive layer and the ZnO nanod array on flexible transparent substrats is a promising approach for the development of high-efficiency and flexible solar cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study demonstrates that it is possible to fabricate flexible organic/inorganic hybrid bulk heterojunction solar cells with a high efficiency on flexible transparent substrat
the flexible hybrid solar cells fabricated in this work are expected to be a potential alternative for flexible solar cells.
the flexible organic/inorganic hybrid photovoltaic device with ZnO nanorods can be a promising candidate for the future flexible solar cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the flexible organic/inorganic hybrid photovoltaic devices based on the combination of ZnO nanocrystal thin film and ZnO nanocrystalline array are promising for flexible and low cost solar cell applications.
the ZnO nanowire array can be used as a scaffold for infiltration of conjugated polymer and fullerene blend solution, which can be applied for flexible organic solar cells.

the flexible hybrid solar cell based on the ZnO nanowire array and the bulk-heterojunction structured organic photoactive layer has a potential to be applied to a flexible solar cell device for the future.
